title: The listener leak
context: A developer asked an AI assistant to track the window width in a React component for a responsive layout decision. The suggested code works initially, but after the component re-renders a few times, the resize handler starts firing multiple times per resize and the app slows down.
question: Why does the resize handler fire more and more times as the component re-renders?
options: The effect has no dependency array, so it re-runs after every render and adds a brand new listener each time without ever removing the old ones.
window.addEventListener silently ignores duplicate listeners, so this can't actually be the cause.
setWidth triggers a re-render loop that has nothing to do with the resize event itself.
useEffect only runs once by default, so extra listeners must come from React StrictMode alone.

explanation.theBug: This useEffect has no dependency array, so React re-runs it after every render — and every run calls addEventListener again, stacking a new listener on top of all the previous ones. None of them are ever removed. After several re-renders, a single resize event fires that many separate handlers, each calling setWidth and triggering yet another render, compounding the problem.
explanation.whyAIGeneratesThis: The core addEventListener call is correct and the effect body is syntactically complete, so the code looks finished. Cleanup functions are an easy detail to omit because the component still works in a quick test — the leak only compounds visibly after several re-renders, which a fast manual check rarely triggers.

theFix.commentary: Always return a cleanup function that removes exactly the listener that was added, and add an empty dependency array so the effect only runs once.

explanation.reviewHeuristic: Every addEventListener, subscription, timer, or interval inside a useEffect needs a matching cleanup function — no exceptions, even if the bug isn't visible in a quick test.
